items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I would play a little drums with Jack Starling at the piano... There is no need to mention the names of the musicians I had in this group except Jack Starling my pianist for a long time

ctx.x: The first of July was a Wednesday and there must have been a crowd of 10 people that night. And they didn't stay more than one and a half hour because the waiters would stand by their tables, and as most of the people drinking white vine, as soon as a glass was empty, the waiter was filling it up and a bottle can go very fast amongst four or five people. The waiters really rushed the people to drink and the people rushed to get out of the joint and that left us playing for the waiters and the cashier who didn't…

I saw the owner of the club once, and that was when we opened. But he was there every night until ten o'clock. The bad business that the place did, didn't seem to worry him. He was the manager of a boxer named Muller who was quite well known in Germany. He would play poker every night in another room until ten, and then he would disappear. The cashier was a woman, and she was in chrage of everything. We worked eight hours and had two fifteen minutes rest periods. And as there was supposed to be continuous music,…

The most that ever came to the joint was one Saturday when there were at least 150 of them at 11 o'clock. At 2'30, the waiters had chased them all away, except a couple of fellows at the bar. At 8p.m. when we went to work, the sun was still shinning, and when we finished at 4.a.m., day was breaking, and the only happy things living seemed to be birds that we heard singing. No one ever came to me and told me that they were jazz fans, and I know there were some in town because was a place not far from where I was…
